Defect Title: Public Unauthenticated Read Access to Orders Collection
Original Failure Scenario & Reproduction: 1. Query collection(db, 'orders') from unauthenticated browser console. 2. Observe all customer order docs returned.
Expected Result: Unauthenticated queries rejected by database rules engine; public cannot dump customer orders.
Actual Result Post-Remediation: Read access denied by Firestore rules engine. Read permitted only when isAuthenticated() && (isAdmin() || request.auth.uid == resource.data.customerUid).
New Verification Evidence: Automated test SEC-001 PASS; firestore.rules lines 636-641 inspected; automated unit test passes.
Remaining Risks / Limitations: Public order tracking uses order number lookup; guest checkout relies on backend reference.

Defect Title: Arbitrary Admin Privilege Escalation via Unrestricted admins Collection Write Access
Original Failure Scenario & Reproduction: 1. Create regular user account. 2. Call setDoc(doc(db, 'admins', user.uid), { role: 'admin', isActive: true }). 3. User becomes full admin.
Expected Result: Writes to /admins collection rejected unless caller is verified active admin.
Actual Result Post-Remediation: Writes to /admins/{adminId} rejected for regular users. allow create, delete: if isAdmin() enforced on server.
New Verification Evidence: Automated test SEC-002 PASS; firestore.rules lines 593-603 enforce isAdmin() on create/delete.
Remaining Risks / Limitations: Recommend adding Firebase Custom Claims for token-level claims caching in Phase 4.

Defect Title: Silent Order Loss: Checkout Reports Order Success Even If Firestore Database Save Fails
Original Failure Scenario & Reproduction: 1. Trigger network offline / permission error during order submit. 2. addDoc fails. 3. Catch block logs warning and displays 'Order Placed Successfully!'; cart cleared.
Expected Result: Order submission halts on Firestore failure, cart items preserved, user presented with retry alert.
Actual Result Post-Remediation: addDoc is mandatory and blocking. Errors trigger setErrorMessage, halt execution, preserve cart items, and notify user.
New Verification Evidence: Automated test ORD-001 PASS; CheckoutPage.jsx lines 126-150 inspected; simulated failure halts flow.
Remaining Risks / Limitations: Network offline queuing via IndexedDB recommended for degraded mobile connections.

Defect Title: Missing Essential HTTP Security Headers in Production (Clickjacking, MIME Sniffing, CSP Risks)
Original Failure Scenario & Reproduction: 1. Inspect curl -I on production Vercel deployment. 2. Observe missing CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options.
Expected Result: All critical HTTP security headers returned by server edge nodes.
Actual Result Post-Remediation: vercel.json configures Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy.
New Verification Evidence: Automated test SEC-003 PASS; vercel.json verified; edge routing rules tested.
Remaining Risks / Limitations: Audit third-party scripts before modifying CSP connect-src.

Defect Title: Missing Cloud Storage Security Rules Specification & Client-Side Only MIME Validation

Expected Result: Storage rules require authenticated user, valid image MIME type, and <5MB file size limit.
Actual Result Post-Remediation: storage.rules created, referenced in firebase.json, enforcing request.auth != null, image/(jpeg|jpg|png|webp), and size < 5MB.
New Verification Evidence: Automated test SEC-004 PASS; storage.rules and firebase.json verified; rule syntax validated.
Remaining Risks / Limitations: Consider background cloud function for automated virus scanning on storage uploads.

Defect Title: Massive Uncompressed Image Payload (>193MB Total, 2MB-3.5MB Per Asset) Degrading Mobile Performance

Expected Result: Image assets compressed to WebP/optimized formats; code splitting implemented; bundle < 300kB gzip.

New Verification Evidence: Automated test PERF-001, PERF-002, PERF-003 PASS; production build output verified; 0 broken images.
Remaining Risks / Limitations: Implement responsive srcset for extreme low-bandwidth mobile devices.

Defect Title: Fatal Runtime TypeError in Cart Total Calculation When Item Price Is Undefined or Null
Original Failure Scenario & Reproduction: 1. Add item with missing/null price. 2. Open cart. 3. item.price.toString() throws TypeError; white screen of death.
Expected Result: getCartTotal handles null, undefined, and diverse currency strings defensively without throwing.
Actual Result Post-Remediation: CartContext defensively handles null/undefined using String(price ?? 0).replace(/[^0-9.]/g, '') and returns 0 on missing values.
New Verification Evidence: Automated test CART-001 PASS; unit tests in App.test.js and functional_regression.test.js pass 100%.
Remaining Risks / Limitations: None. Defensive parsing handles all edge cases.
